channel.title: AI Systems Architecture Handbook
channel.description: New and rewritten pages of the AI Systems Architecture Handbook.

item.title: Model Selection and Deployment Models
item.description: How to choose a model configuration per component, decide where and on whose capacity it runs, and route each request without breaking data-class rules.

item.title: Multi-Model Strategy and Model Routing
item.description: How predictive routers and cascades pick a model per request, how to set thresholds from error costs, and how routing fails through drift and cost attacks.

item.title: Hosted API vs. Self-Hosted vs. Hybrid Deployment
item.description: How processing location, operator, and capacity contract separate hosted, provisioned, and self-hosted inference, and how to build a fail-closed hybrid.

item.title: Model Selection Criteria: A Multi-Criteria Method
item.description: How to choose a model per component with hard gates, slice-level evals, load-tested latency, cost per successful task, Pareto filtering, and sensitivity checks.

item.title: The Model Landscape
item.description: How weight control and scale, test-time compute, and input modality each change a model's contract on cost, latency, versioning, and where its errors hide.

item.title: Multimodal Models: Vision, Documents, and Audio
item.description: How images, PDF pages, and audio become tokens, what resolution budgets cost, when native multimodal input beats OCR or ASR pipelines, and how it fails.

item.title: Reasoning Models and Test-Time Compute
item.description: How reasoning models spend hidden output tokens to raise accuracy, what effort controls guarantee, and how to budget latency, cost tails, and opaque state.

item.title: Frontier, Open-Weight, and Small Language Models
item.description: How frontier, open-weight, and small models differ in who controls weights and versions, what runs where, memory and cost math, licensing, and failure modes.

item.title: Foundations: The Architectural Nature of AI Systems
item.description: The component model and the failure and fitness decisions that every later part assumes, from correctness as a rate to evidence that survives production.

item.title: Failure Modes and Fitness for Purpose
item.description: How to classify what goes wrong in model-backed systems, decide whether a model belongs on a task, and tell a convincing prototype from evidence of reliability.

item.title: From Demo to Production: Why AI Prototypes Mislead
item.description: How the prototype loop manufactures optimistic evidence through chosen inputs, tuning, lenient grading, and a hidden operator, and which evidence replaces it.

item.title: When AI Is the Wrong Solution: A Decision Framework
item.description: A gated procedure for deciding whether a task should use an LLM, rules, classical ML, or people, from input openness, error tolerance, checkability, and cost.

item.title: A Taxonomy of AI Failure Modes
item.description: How to classify LLM system failures by origin layer, detectability, and consequence, triage them from recorded traces, and map them to OWASP, NIST, and MAST.

item.title: The AI Component Model
item.description: What kind of component an LLM is, how tokens, context, and sampling shape its behavior, and why a measured quality rate is not the rate production delivers.

item.title: Capability vs. Reliability: Closing the Production Gap
item.description: Why benchmark and demo scores overstate delivered quality, how to measure pass^k and worst-slice rates, and how scope, checks, and abstention close it.

item.title: Anatomy of an LLM as a System Component: Tokens, Context, Sampling
item.description: How tokenization, a stateless bounded context window, and the sample-append-stop loop set the cost, latency, limits, and failure modes of every LLM call.

item.title: Deterministic vs. Probabilistic Systems: What Changes for Architecture
item.description: How contracts, retries, caching, testing, versioning, and auditing change when a component returns a sample from a distribution instead of a computed result.

item.title: Tool Call Idempotency, Retry, and Compensation
item.description: Why agents duplicate side effects through retries and re-planning, how to derive idempotency keys from intent, and how to compensate a half-executed plan.
